XTS API

XTS API (Xtreme Trading System API) is a complete trading framework that connects your application directly to brokers and stock exchanges — enabling market data, order management, portfolio services, and real-time updates.

Secure authentication Place & manage orders Portfolio & holdings Real-time WebSocket Live market quotes Easy integration

docs.title: What is XTS API?
docs.text:
XTS API acts as a bridge between your application and the stock exchange. It separates into two independent channels — Market Data (read-only feeds) and Interactive (two-way trading operations) — so network traffic never interferes with your orders.

Market Data APIRead-only market information

  • Historical price data
  • Market depth (order book)

  • WebSocket quote streaming
Interactive APITwo-way trading operations

  • Place / Modify / Cancel orders
  • Holdings & positions

docs.title: About RMoney
docs.text:
RMoney is a technology-driven stock broking and investment platform that provides traders and investors with access to financial markets through modern trading applications, desktop platforms, and APIs.

RMoney enables users to trade across multiple market segments including Equity, Futures & Options (F&O), Currency, and Commodities. Along with manual trading, RMoney also provides API-based trading infrastructure that allows developers and traders to build custom applications, automate trading strategies, and access market data programmatically.

docs.title: What are RMoney APIs?
docs.text:
RMoney APIs are a collection of developer interfaces that allow applications to communicate directly with the RMoney trading ecosystem. Instead of placing orders manually, developers can use APIs to perform actions automatically.

  • Retrieve live market prices
  • Access historical market data
  • Place buy and sell orders
  • Track positions and holdings
  • Monitor portfolios
  • Receive real-time market updates
  • Build algorithmic trading systems

These APIs are based on the Symphony XTS framework and are designed for high-speed trading and market data access.

Getting Started📘 The Complete Reference Manual: Symphony XTS API v2 & Python Client Library

Welcome! This is a comprehensive, standalone guide designed for new users and programmers to master the Symphony XTS Front-End API (v2.0) and its official Python client library, xts-api-client.

No prior experience with trading APIs is required. We explain everything from high-level architecture to low-level parameters, supplemented by visual diagrams and code examples.

1. High-Level Concepts & Mental Models What is XTS?

Symphony XTS is a high-speed trading system interface. It sits between your custom software (trading bot, dashboard, or scanner) and the stock brokers/exchanges (like NSE, BSE, MCX).

The Two-Channel Split (Dual Engine)

To prevent network traffic jams, XTS separates commands into two entirely independent channels:

  • Interactive API : Private and secure. Used to place trades, check cash balances, query open positions, and get instant notifications when your orders fill.
  • Market Data API : Public and read-only. Used to fetch stock names, request historical candle data, and stream real-time price updates (LTP, bid/ask spreads). 2. Technical Vocabulary & Business Rules

    Before writing code, you must understand the terminology used in API parameters:

    A. Exchange Segments

    Tells XTS which market segment you are querying:

    • NSECM (1): National Stock Exchange Cash Market (Buying actual shares of Reliance, TCS, etc.)
    • NSEFO (2):National Stock Exchange Futures & Options (Trading Nifty options/futures)
    • NSECD (3): National Stock Exchange Currency Derivatives (USD/INR trading)
    • MCXFO (51): Multi Commodity Exchange Futures & Options (Gold, Silver, Crude Oil)
    • BSECM (11) & BSEFO (12): Bombay Stock Exchange equivalents
    B. Product Types

    Tells the broker how to manage the trade margin and holding period:

    • MIS (Margin Intraday Square-off): Closed automatically before market shuts. Offers high leverage.
    • NRML (Normal): Used to hold futures & options contracts for multiple days.
    • CNC (Cash and Carry): Used to buy actual stock shares for long-term investing. No leverage.
    C. Order Types
    • MARKET: Buys/sells immediately at the best available current market price.
    • LIMIT: Executes only at your specified price or better.
    • STOPMARKET: Triggered when the market price hits a target trigger price, then executes as a Market order.
    • STOPLIMIT: Triggered when the market price hits a target trigger price, then places a Limit order.
    D. Time In Force (Validity)
    • DAY: The order is valid until the market closes today.
    • IOC (Immediate or Cancel): The order must execute instantly, or any unfilled part is cancelled.
    • FOK (Fill or Kill): The entire order must execute instantly in full, or the whole order is cancelled.
    3. Library Architecture & File Structure

    Here is a map of the xts-api-client package, detailing what each file does: 4. REST API Reference: Authentication & Session

    Every action requires a session token. Here is the lifecycle of an XTS session:

    --- 5. Interactive API (Trading Operations)

    The Interactive client manages your money, orders, and positions.

    A. Order Placement & The Order Lifecycle

    When you submit an order, it moves through a state machine inside the exchange:

    B. Order Parameters Deep Dive

    When calling place_order(), you must specify the following parameters:

    response = await client.place_order(
    exchangeSegment="NSECM",           # "NSECM", "NSEFO", "MCXFO"
    exchangeInstrumentID=2885,         # Numeric code for the stock (e.g. 2885 for RELIANCE)
    productType="MIS",                 # "MIS" (Intraday), "NRML" (F&O Carryover), "CNC" (Equity Delivery)
    orderType="LIMIT",                 # "MARKET", "LIMIT", "STOPMARKET", "STOPLIMIT"
    orderSide="BUY",                   # "BUY" or "SELL"
    timeInForce="DAY",                 # "DAY", "IOC"
    disclosedQuantity=0,               # Quantity visible to public order book (0 hides nothing)
    orderQuantity=10,                  # Total quantity to buy/sell
    limitPrice=2450.50,                # Price to execute (required if LIMIT or STOPLIMIT)
    stopPrice=0.0,                     # Trigger price (required if STOPMARKET or STOPLIMIT)
    orderUniqueIdentifier="my_bot_01"  # Custom string tag to track this specific order
)
    C. Advanced Order Types (Cover & Bracket) 1. Cover Orders (CO)

    A Cover Order has a stop-loss order chained directly to it. It is highly leveraged and requires an entry transaction and a trigger price (the stop-loss activation level).

    1. Entry Order(Market or Limit) If Filled ⟶ 2. Stop Loss triggerPrice(Active on Exchange) If price hits Trigger level ⟶ 3. Executed Exit(Market Order)

    Cover Order Parameters & Code:

    # Place a Cover Order: Buy Reliance at market, stop-loss trigger active at ₹2400
co_response = await client.place_cover_order(
    exchangeSegment="NSECM",
    exchangeInstrumentID=2885,
    orderSide="BUY",
    orderType="MARKET",
    orderQuantity=5,
    disclosedQuantity=0,
    limitPrice=0.0,                    # 0.0 because orderType is MARKET
    stopPrice=2400.0,                  # Stop Loss Trigger level
    orderUniqueIdentifier="co_trade_01"
)
    2. Bracket Orders (BO)

    A Bracket Order surrounds your entry order with two bracket legs: a Take Profit Target and a Stop-Loss Protection. Both exit orders are sent to the exchange as a One-Cancels-the-Other (OCO) pair.

    Bracket Order Parameters & Code:

    # Place a Bracket Order: Buy Reliance at ₹2450. Sell at ₹2500 for profit (+50) or ₹2420 for loss (-30)
bo_response = await client.place_bracketorder(
    exchangeSegment="NSECM",
    exchangeInstrumentID=2885,
    orderType="LIMIT",
    orderSide="BUY",
    disclosedQuantity=0,
    orderQuantity=10,
    limitPrice=2450.00,
    squarOff=50.0,                     # Profit target offset (added to entry price)
    stopLossPrice=30.0,                # Stop-Loss protection offset (subtracted from entry price)
    trailingStoploss=0.0,              # 0.0 means inactive. Set value to adjust SL up as price rises
    isProOrder=False,                  # Set True for proprietary trading accounts
    orderUniqueIdentifier="bo_trade_01"
)
    D. Spread & GTT Orders 1. Spread Orders

    Spread orders let you trade price differences between two stock options or futures contracts simultaneously (e.g. buying July Futures and selling August Futures).

    • Place Spread: POST /interactive/orders/spread
    • Modify Spread: PUT /interactive/orders/spread
    • Cancel Spread: DELETE /interactive/orders/spread
    2. GTT (Good-Till-Triggered) Orders

    GTT orders remain active in the system for weeks or months until a target trigger price is hit. Once hit, it launches a standard order.

    • Place GTT: POST /interactive/orders/gtt
    • GTT Order Book: GET /interactive/orders/gtt/orderbook
    • Cancel GTT: DELETE /interactive/orders/gtt
    E. Portfolio Management & Positions

    Once you have active trades, you query your balances and positions:

    async def query_portfolio(client):
    # 1. Available margin and cash balance
    balance = await client.get_balance()
    available_cash = balance['result']['BalanceList'][0]['limitObject']['RMSSubLimits']['cashAvailable']
    print(f"Available Cash: ₹{available_cash}")

    # 2. Holdings (Long-term stocks held in your demat account)
    holdings = await client.get_holding()
    print("Holdings List:", holdings['result'])

    # 3. Daywise positions (Today's trading activity)
    day_pos = await client.get_position_daywise()

    # 4. Netwise positions (Current active net open positions)
    net_pos = await client.get_position_netwise()
    for pos in net_pos['result']:
        print(f"Instrument: {pos['ExchangeInstrumentID']} | Open Qty: {pos['NetQty']} | MTM PnL: ₹{pos['MTM']}")

    # 5. Convert Position (e.g., convert Intraday 'MIS' to Delivery 'CNC')
    await client.convert_position(
        exchangeSegment="NSECM",
        exchangeInstrumentID=2885,
        targetQty=5,
        isDayWise=True,
        oldProductType="MIS",
        newProductType="CNC"
    )
    F. Margin Calculator APIs

    You can request how much cash margin is required to place or modify orders before actually sending them:

    • Regular Margin: POST /interactive/margin/regular
    • Cover Margin: POST /interactive/margin/cover
    • Bracket Margin: POST /interactive/margin/bracket
    --- 6. Market Data API (Feeds & Queries)

    The Market Data client fetches historical chart candles, instrument identifiers, and subscriptions.

    async def query_market_data(market_client):
    # 1. Search for a security by trading symbol
    search_resp = await market_client.search_by_scriptname("TATAMOTORS")
    instrument_id = search_resp['result'][0]['ExchangeInstrumentID']
    print(f"TATA Motors Instrument ID: {instrument_id}")

    # 2. Query Expiry Dates for Options/Futures contracts
    expiries = await market_client.get_expiry_date(
        exchangeSegment=2,             # NSEFO
        series="OPTIDX",               # Index Option
        symbol="NIFTY"
    )
    print("Nifty Option Expiries:", expiries['result'])

    # 3. Retrieve Historical Chart Candles (OHLC)
    candles = await market_client.get_ohlc(
        exchangeSegment=1,             # NSECM
        exchangeInstrumentID=22,       # NIFTY Index
        startTime="Jun 01 2026 091500",  # MMM DD YYYY HHMMSS
        endTime="Jun 15 2026 153000",
        compressionValue=5             # 5-minute intervals
    )
    print("Raw Candle Data:", candles['result']['dataReponse'][:200])
    7. Real-time Socket Streaming (WebSockets via Socket.IO)

    WebSockets establish a constant, open channel of communication. Data flows automatically without your software having to ask for it.

    Step 1: Connection URL Breakdown

    The library connects to the socket using a specific query string:

    • Interactive Socket: {root_url}/?token={token}&userID={userID}&apiType=INTERACTIVE
    • Market Data Socket: {root_url}/?token={token}&userID={userID}&publishFormat=JSON&broadcastMode=Full
    Step 2: The Event Code Map

    The Market Data socket streams message packets prefixed with numeric event codes:

    Step 3: Complete WebSocket Listener Implementation

    To catch these events, you subclass MarketDataSocketClient (for prices) or InteractiveSocketClient (for trading updates) and assign it to the socket managers:

    import asyncio
from xts_api_client.xts_connect_async import XTSConnect
from xts_api_client.market_data_socket import MDSocket_io
from xts_api_client.market_data_socket_client import MarketDataSocketClient

# 1. Create your listener implementation
class RealTimePriceFeed(MarketDataSocketClient):
    async def on_connect(self):
        print(" Connected to live price feeds!")

    async def on_disconnect(self):
        print(" Socket disconnected!")

    async def on_error(self, data):
        print(" Error from Socket:", data)

    # Event 1512: LTP Ticks
    async def on_event_last_traded_price_full(self, data):
        print(f"Price Tick -> ID: {data['ExchangeInstrumentID']} | Price: ₹{data['LastTradedPrice']}")

    # Event 1501: Bid/Ask Depth Ticks
    async def on_event_touchline_full(self, data):
        print(f"Spread -> Bid: {data['BidInfo']['Price']} | Ask: {data['AskInfo']['Price']}")

# 2. Main initialization script
async def stream_prices():
    # Login HTTP first
    client = XTSConnect(
        apiKey="your_market_key",
        secretKey="your_market_secret",
        source="WEBAPI",
        root="https://api.yourbroker.com"
    )
    await client.marketdata_login()

    # Assign socket listener
    listener = RealTimePriceFeed()
    socket_client = MDSocket_io(
        token=client.token,
        userID=client.userID,
        root_url=client.root,
        marketdatasocketclient=listener
    )

    # Establish connection
    await socket_client.connect()

    # Subscribe to Reliance (2885) and Nifty (22)
    instruments = [
        {"exchangeSegment": 1, "exchangeInstrumentID": 2885},
        {"exchangeSegment": 1, "exchangeInstrumentID": 22}
    ]
    await client.send_subscription(Instruments=instruments, xtsMessageCode=1512)

    # Keep the program running to see ticks stream
    await asyncio.sleep(20)

    # Clean up
    await socket_client.disconnect()
    await client.marketdata_logout()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(stream_prices())
    8. Mark-To-Market (MTM) PnL Calculations

    Symphony calculates your unrealized profit or loss (PnL) in real-time. Here is how the math works:

    Total PnL = Realized PnL + Unrealized PnL Realized PnL

    Realized PnL is locked in when you complete a trade loop (Buy and Sell the same contract).

    Realized PnL = (Sell Price − Buy Price) × Traded Quantity Unrealized PnL

    Unrealized PnL fluctuates as the market price moves. It is calculated on open positions:

    • For Long Positions (Open Quantity > 0): Unrealized PnL = (Current LTP − Average Buy Price) × Open Quantity
    • For Short Positions (Open Quantity < 0): Unrealized PnL = (Average Sell Price − Current LTP) × Open Quantity (Absolute)
    9. Helper Library Utilities

    The client library includes xts_api_client.helper.helper to parse and manage incoming data structures automatically.

    1. Master List Parser (Pandas DataFrame)

    Symphony sends large stock master files as pipeline-separated string streams. The helper converts them to clean Pandas dataframes:

    from xts_api_client.helper.helper import cm_master_string_to_df, fo_master_string_to_df

# Assume 'raw_csv_response' is retrieved from get_master() call
df_equities = cm_master_string_to_df(raw_csv_response)
# You can now run pandas queries
print(df_equities[df_equities['Name'] == 'RELIANCE'])
    2. MS-DOS Time Zone Converter

    Exchange times are given as seconds elapsed since the MS-DOS Epoch (1980-01-01). The helper translates this to standard Unix nanoseconds:

    from xts_api_client.helper.helper import dostime_secomds_to_unixtime

unix_nanoseconds = dostime_secomds_to_unixtime(1464972900)
print("Standard Unix timestamp:", unix_nanoseconds)
    3. Account-Wide Squareoff Helper

    The helper provides a routine to retrieve all your open positions and instantly exit them at market price to protect capital in emergencies:

    from xts_api_client.helper.helper import async_squareoff_all_positions_

# Retrieve all positions and close them out
sq_off_ids = await async_squareoff_all_positions_(interactive_client)
print("Emergency Squared off Order IDs:", sq_off_ids)
    10. Robust Code Design: Reconnections & Retries

    To deploy algorithms safely, you must handle network disconnects or API timeouts. Here is a production-grade template for a Gateway wrapper that you can copy to build your systems:

    import asyncio
import logging
from xts_api_client.xts_connect_async import XTSConnect
from xts_api_client.interactive_socket import OrderSocket_io
from xts_api_client.interactive_socket_client import InteractiveSocketClient
from httpx import PoolTimeout, ConnectTimeout, ReadTimeout

class OrderCallbackHandler(InteractiveSocketClient):
    def __init__(self, gateway):
        self.gateway = gateway

    async def on_connect(self):
        self.gateway.connected = True
        logging.info("WebSocket connected!")

    async def on_disconnect(self):
        self.gateway.connected = False
        logging.warning("WebSocket lost! Reconnecting...")
        asyncio.create_task(self.gateway.reconnect())

class XTSGateway:
    def __init__(self, api_url, key, secret):
        self.api_url = api_url
        self.key = key
        self.secret = secret
        self.client = None
        self.socket = None
        self.connected = False

    async def connect(self):
        # 1. Login REST API
        self.client = XTSConnect(self.key, self.secret, "WEBAPI", self.api_url)
        await self.client.interactive_login()

        # 2. Start WebSocket Connection
        self.socket = OrderSocket_io(
            token=self.client.token,
            userID=self.client.userID,
            root_url=self.client.root,
            reconnection=True,
            interactiveSocketClient=OrderCallbackHandler(self)
        )
        await self.socket.connect()

    async def place_order_safe(self, params: dict, retries=4):
        """Places orders with auto-retry on HTTP timeouts"""
        for attempt in range(retries):
            try:
                response = await self.client.place_order(**params)
                return response
            except (PoolTimeout, ConnectTimeout, ReadTimeout) as timeout_exc:
                logging.warning(f"Timeout on attempt {attempt+1}/{retries}. Retrying...")
                await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
        raise RuntimeError("Failed to place order: Connection Timed Out")

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
Keep Secrets Secure

Store API secrets only in backend environment variables. Never commit them to code repositories or expose them in frontend apps.

Always Use HTTPS

All API calls must use https://. Plain HTTP exposes your token to network interception and man-in-the-middle attacks.

Rotate Tokens Regularly

Do not use the same token indefinitely. Refresh access tokens before they expire and immediately revoke compromised tokens.

Validate Before Requesting

docs.title: Cover Orders
docs.text:
Cover Orders

A Cover Order (CO) is a special order that combines a main order with a compulsory stop-loss — giving you built-in risk protection and higher leverage in a single placement.

Built-in stop-loss Higher leverage Automatic risk management Intraday trading Reduced monitoring Faster execution

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text:
URL

POST https://developers.symphonyfintech.in/1interactive/orders/cover ⧉ Copy

docs.title: What is a Cover Order?
docs.text:
A Cover Order lets you enter a trade with a mandatory stop-loss baked in. Because the broker knows your maximum possible loss upfront, they offer higher leverage — making CO ideal for active intraday traders who want capital efficiency without manual exit monitoring.

Main Order
  • Buys or sells the stock
  • Executed immediately at market
  • Entry price defined here
Stop-Loss Order
  • Placed automatically alongside
  • Triggers if price moves against you
  • Exits position to cap the loss

docs.title: How It Works — Example
docs.text: RELIANCE — BUY Cover Order ORDER DETAILS Buy Price₹2,850 Stop Loss₹2,830 Quantity100 shares Max Risk₹20 × 100 = ₹2,000 OUTCOMES Price rises → ₹2,900Profit = ₹50 × 100 = ₹5,000 Price drops → ₹2,830SL triggered — Loss capped at ₹2,000

docs.title: Cover Order Workflow
docs.text: User Places Order → Main Order Executed → Stop-Loss Created → Market Moves → Profit or SL Triggered → Position Closed

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
Mandatory Stop Loss

Every CO must have a stop-loss. It cannot be placed without one.

Higher Margin Benefit

Because risk is predefined, brokers offer more leverage for Cover Orders.

Automatic Risk Management

Stop-loss triggers automatically — no need to manually watch the market.

Intraday Only

Cover Orders are squared off automatically before market close.

Faster Execution

Predefined risk parameters allow the system to execute orders more efficiently.

docs.title: Advantages vs Limitations
docs.text:
Advantages
  • Reduced risk with automatic protection
  • Higher leverage from broker
  • Better capital utilisation
  • No manual exit needed for losses
  • Suitable for active traders
Limitations
  • Stop-loss is mandatory — cannot skip
  • Available for intraday trading only
  • Main order and SL are linked
  • SL rejection may force broker square-off
  • Not supported on all instruments

Instead of sending long descriptive text, APIs use short codes internally. For example:

docs.title: 2. ProductType
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description MIS 1          - Margin Intraday Square-off         - Intraday trading product type where positions must be squared off before market close. Provides higher leverage compared to delivery.         - MIS is used for same-day trading only called Intraday Trading.         - All trades must be closed before the market closes (9:15 AM – 3:30 PM).         - The broker gives extra money (leverage), so you can trade with a larger amount.         - If you don't close the trade, the broker will automatically close it before market close.         - After closing the trade, the broker takes back its money, and you keep your money along with any profit (or bear any loss).          NRML 2          - Normal         - Standard product type used for carrying forward positions overnight in derivatives or cash without compulsory intraday square-off.         - NRML is used to keep trades overnight or for multiple days.         - You do not need to close the trade on the same day.         - It is mainly used for Futures and Options (F&O) trading.         - You can hold the trade until the contract expiry date; after expiry, the position expires or is settled automatically.         - Brokers also provide leverage in NRML, but it is usually lower than the leverage available in MIS.          CNC 4          - Cash And Carry          - Delivery-based product type for equity trades. Shares are delivered to the Demat account, with no leverage.         - CNC is used for real stock delivery and long-term investing.         - Trades are done using your own money, with little or no leverage.         - It is mainly used for buying and selling shares (equity).         - There is no need to close the position on the same day.         - You can hold the shares for as long as you want, such as days, months, or even years.          CO 8          - Cover Order         - CO is mainly used for intraday (same-day) trading.         - Intraday order type where a market or limit order is placed along with a mandatory stop-loss order. Provides higher leverage while controlling risk.         - It focuses on safety and risk control.         - A stop-loss (loss limit) order is compulsory with every trade.         - Brokers usually provide higher leverage because the risk is controlled.         - If the market moves against you and reaches the stop-loss price, the trade is automatically exited to limit the loss.          BO 16 - Bracket Order - Advanced order type where a main order is placed with both a target (profit booking) and stop-loss. Once one is executed, the other is automatically cancelled. Can also include a trailing stop-loss. - BO focuses on both profit target and stop-loss. - It is used to balance profit and loss automatically. - It contains three orders: Entry Order, Target Profit Order, and Stop-Loss Order. - When the market reaches either the target price or the stop-loss price, the trade exits automatically. - It is mainly used for intraday trading and helps traders manage risk and profit together. MTF 32          - Margin Trading Faciity - Allows investors to buy stocks by partly paying upfront and borrowing the balance from the broker. Shares can be carried forward as long as margin requirements are met.         - MTF is used for buying shares with the help of money borrowed from the broker.         - The broker charges interest on the borrowed amount.         - You can hold the shares for as long as you want, such as days, months, or even years.         - The borrowed amount remains with the broker, and interest is charged until it is repaid.         - It allows you to buy more shares than you could using only your own money.

docs.title: 3. OrderType
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description Market 1          - Market Order         - An order to buy or sell immediately at the best available price in the market.         - A Market Order is executed immediately at the current market price.         - You only specify the quantity to buy or sell; the price is decided by the market.         - It is used when quick execution is more important than getting a specific price.         - Example: If TCS is trading around ₹3500 and you place a Market Buy Order, it will be executed immediately at the best available market price.          Limit 2          -  Limit Order          - An order to buy or sell at a specified price (or better).         - In a Limit Order, you set the price at which you want to buy or sell.         - The trade is executed only if the market reaches your specified price or a better price.         - It is used when getting a specific price is more important than immediate execution. - Example: If the current TCS price is ₹3500 and you place a Buy Limit Order at ₹3480, the order will execute only if TCS falls to ₹3480 or below; otherwise, it will remain pending.          StopMarket 4          - StopMarket Order         - An order that becomes a market order once a specified trigger price is reached. Used mainly to limit losses.         - In a Stop Market Order, you set a trigger price (stop price).         - When the market reaches the trigger price, the order becomes a Market Order and is executed immediately at the best available price.         - It is mainly used to limit losses or protect profits automatically. - Example: If you bought TCS at ₹3500 and set a Stop Market Sell Order with a trigger price of ₹3480, then when TCS falls to ₹3480, the order is activated and the shares are sold immediately at the current market price.          StopLimit 8          - StopLimit Order         - An order that becomes a limit order once the trigger price is reached. It executes only at the specified limit price or better.         - In a Stop Limit Order, you set both a trigger price and a limit price.         - When the market reaches the trigger price, a Limit Order is placed at the specified limit price.         - It is used to control the execution price while limiting losses or protecting profits. - Example: If you bought TCS at ₹3500, you can set a trigger price of ₹3480 and a limit price of ₹3475. When TCS reaches ₹3480, a sell order at ₹3475 is placed. The trade will execute only at ₹3475 or a better price.          OCO 32          - One Cancels the Other         - A conditional order where two linked orders are placed — if one gets executed, the other is automatically cancelled.         - OCO contains two orders together, usually a Target Order and a Stop-Loss Order.         - It helps you manage both profit and loss automatically.         - When one order is executed, the other order is automatically cancelled.         - It is useful when you want to set both a profit target and a loss limit without monitoring the market continuously.          MTF 32          - Margin Trading Facility         - MTF allows you to buy shares using money borrowed from the broker.         - You can hold the shares for a long time (days, months, or years); there is no need to close the trade on the same day          - The broker charges interest on the borrowed amount until it is repaid.         - It helps you buy more shares than you could with only your own money.

Used when exiting a long position or initiating a short position (expecting the price to fall).             - You sell when you expect the price to go down or when you want to book profit.             - Profit is made if you buy back later at a lower price (short selling) or if you sell shares you already own at a higher price.

docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description DAY 1              - Day Order             - The order remains active only for the current trading day.             - If the order is not executed by market close, it is automatically cancelled.             - Order remains valid only for the trading day. If not executed by market close, it is cancelled automatically.              GTC 2              - Good Till Cancelled             - The order remains active until you cancel it manually.             - It can stay active for many days if it is not executed.             - The order is cancelled only when you manually cancel it.              IOC 4              - Immediate Or Cancel             - The order must be executed immediately.             - If only some quantity can be executed, the remaining quantity is cancelled instantly.             - Any unfilled part of the order does not stay pending.             - Example: If you place an IOC order to buy 100 shares and only 60 shares are available, those 60 shares are bought immediately and the remaining 40 shares are cancelled. docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description Open or New 48              - Open/New means a new order has been placed and is waiting to be executed.             - The order is active in the market but has not been fully or partially traded yet.             - The order can later be executed, modified, or cancelled.              PartiallyFilled 49              - PartiallyFilled Order             - It means only some part of the order has been executed.The remaining quantity is still active and waiting to be executed.             - The order stays open until the remaining quantity is filled or cancelled.              Filled 50              - Filled Order             - Filled means the order has been completely executed.             - All the requested quantity has been bought or sold successfully.              Cancelled 52              - Cancelled Order             - Cancelled means the order has been cancelled and will not be executed.             - The order may be cancelled by you, the broker, or the exchange.             - No quantity will be traded after the order is cancelled.              Replaced 53              - Replaced Order             - Replaced means an existing order has been modified or updated.             - The old order is replaced with a new one having the updated details.Changes may include price, quantity, or other order parameters.              PendingCancel 54              - PendingCancel Order             - PendingCancel means a cancellation request has been sent, but the order has not been cancelled yet.             - The system or exchange is processing the cancellation request.The order status will change to Cancelled once the cancellation is completed.          Rejected 56              - Rejected Order             - Rejected means the order was not accepted by the exchange or broker.             - The order is not executed and becomes inactive.             - Common reasons include insufficient funds, invalid price, or trading restrictions. EnterpriseWeb 154              - EnterpriseWeb means the order was placed through an enterprise or institutional web platform.             - It is typically used by organizations, brokers, or large clients rather than individual retail traders.             - Orders can be placed and managed through a specialized web-based interface.             - Example: If a mutual fund or a corporate client places an order through the broker's enterprise web portal, the order source will be EnterpriseWeb. docs.title: 8. Position Square Off Mode
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description DayWise 1              - DayWise means positions or statistics are calculated separately for each trading day.             - Only the trades done on the current day are considered.             - At the end of the day, the values are reset for the next trading day.             - Example: If you buy and sell 100 TCS shares today, the profit/loss will be shown only for today's trades under DayWise.**              NetWise 2              - NetWise means all trades are combined together to show the overall (net) position.             - It considers both previous and current trades instead of only today's trades.             - It shows your total quantity, average price, and overall profit/loss.             - Example: If you bought 100 TCS shares yesterday and 50 more today, NetWise will show a total position of 150 shares.**

docs.title: 9. Position Square Off Quantity Type
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description Percentage 0              - Percentage means values are shown in percentage (%) instead of actual numbers.             - It helps compare profit, loss, growth, or performance easily.             - The result is displayed as a percentage of the total value. ExactQty 1              - ExactQty means the exact quantity requested must be executed.             - The order will not be partially filled.             - If the full quantity is not available, the order may remain pending or fail based on the order rules.

docs.title: 10. MarketType
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description Normal 1              - Normal means regular trading.             - It is the standard order type used for normal buy and sell transactions.             - No special conditions or restrictions are applied to the order.              Oddlot 2              - It means the order is an odd lot type             - It is used when quantity is less than the standard trading lot size             - These are small or non-standard share quantities (not full lots)             - It is treated separately from normal lot trading in the system.Useful for small quantity or partial share trading orders             - Example:                 • Suppose the normal trading lot size is 100 shares                 • A trader places an order for 25 shares of Reliance Industries                 • Since 25 is less than the standard lot size (100), it is treated as an Odd Lot order                 • In the system/API, this order will be marked as: Oddlot = 2              RetailDebt 3              - represents a retail debt order type             - It is used for buying/selling debt instruments like bonds or government securities             - These trades are done by retail (individual) investors, not big institutions             - It usually involves small investment amounts              Auction 4              - represents orders placed in an auction market             - It is used when securities are traded through a bidding process instead of normal trading             - Buyers and sellers submit bids, and the best price gets matched             - It is often used in special cases like exchange auctions or settlement auctions              CallAuction1 5              - represents a specific call auction order type (Phase 1)             - Used to find a single fair market price by matching many buy and sell orders at once.             - Orders are first collected, then the system calculates one price, and finally trades are executed together in one batch.              CallAuction2 6              - means a second type of call auction session where orders are not executed instantly.             - Orders are first collected and then a single fair price is discovered by the system.             - After price discovery, all matching buy and sell orders are executed together in one batch.             - it is a batch trading mode where trades happen together at one final auction price.

docs.title: 11. OrderLegStatus
docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description SingleOrderLeg 1        - means the order contains only one trading instruction (one leg).       - It is a regular standalone order, not part of a multi-leg strategy.       - The order is executed independently without being linked to other orders.       - In simple words: one order = one action (buy or sell) on a single instrument. SpreadFirstLeg 2         - means this order is the first leg of a spread strategy.        - A spread strategy consists of two or more linked orders executed together.        - The first leg is the initial buy or sell order in the spread.        - Example: Buy NIFTY July Futures (first leg) and Sell NIFTY August Futures (second leg).        SpreadSecondLeg 3        - means this order is the second leg of a spread strategy.       - It is linked to the first leg and forms part of a multi-leg trade.       - Both legs work together to implement a spread trading strategy. MultilegFirstLeg 4        - means this order is the first leg of a multi-leg trading strategy.       The first leg in a multi-leg strategy (often options).        MultilegSecondLeg 5 The second leg in a multi-leg strategy. MultilegThirdLeg 6 The third leg in advanced multi-leg strategies.

docs.title: Rate Limit
docs.text:
Rate Limiting

Rate limiting controls the number of requests a client can make to an API within a specific time period — maintaining platform stability, ensuring fair usage, and protecting backend services from excessive traffic.

Per-second limits 429 Too Many Requests Rate-limit headers Unified throttle Exponential backoff Fair resource allocation

docs.title: Why Rate Limiting Is Important
docs.text:
Prevent Overload

Stops servers from being overwhelmed during peak traffic periods.

Fair Usage

Ensures equal resource allocation among all users and clients.

Reliability

Maintains consistent API performance and platform availability.

Abuse Protection

Guards against accidental loops, bots, and excessive automation.

docs.title: How Rate Limits Work
docs.text:
Each endpoint is assigned a maximum number of requests allowed per second (RPS). Requests beyond the limit are rejected until the window resets.

✅ Allowed — 10 req/sec limit Request 1  → ✓ Request 2  → ✓ Request 3  → ✓ ⋮ (up to 10) Request 10 → ✓

10 requests within 1 second — accepted

❌ Rejected — 10 req/sec limit Request 1–10 → ✓ Request 11   → ✗ 429 Request 12   → ✗ 429 Request 13   → ✗ 429 Request 14   → ✗ 429

15 requests within 1 second — 5 rejected

docs.title: Rate Limit Response
docs.text:
When the rate limit is exceeded the API returns HTTP 429:

429 Too Many Requests 
{
  "type": "error",
  "code": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
  "description": "Request rate exceeded the allowed limit. Please retry after some time."
}

docs.text:

X-RateLimit-Limit: 10

X-RateLimit-Reset: 1718700000

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Exponential Backoff

On 429, wait 1s → retry. If still failing, wait 2s → 4s → 8s before each retry.

Cache Responses

Cache frequently requested data (e.g., instruments, profile) to avoid redundant API calls.

Monitor Headers

Read X-RateLimit-Remaining before sending batches to stay within limits.

Queue Requests

Queue non-critical requests and spread them over time rather than bursting all at once.

Avoid Polling

Use WebSocket streaming instead of repeatedly polling REST endpoints for updates.

⏱ Respect Retry Intervals

Wait the duration specified by the API in the retry response before re-sending.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Rate limits may vary by endpoint — always check the endpoint-specific table.
  • Limits are subject to change to ensure platform stability.
  • Repeated violations may result in temporary throttling or access restrictions.

Error Codes

When an API request fails, RMoney returns an error code with a message so you can identify the problem and fix it fast. Understanding error codes is essential to building reliable trading applications.

Identify problems quickly without guessing Debug API requests with precise context Handle failures gracefully in your application Improve overall application reliability Basic

docs.text: Your Application API Request RMoney API Success Response Data Failure Error Code + Message

docs.title: Error Response Format
docs.text:
Every error response from the RMoney API follows this consistent structure:

{
  "type":        "error",
  "code":        "InvalidInput",
  "description": "Quantity must be greater than zero",
  "result":      {}
}
type Always "error" when the request fails code Short machine-readable error identifier description Human-readable explanation of the error result Empty object on failure Intermediate

{ "type": "success", "result": { "AppOrderID": 1234 } }

{ "type": "error", "code": "InvalidInput",

{ "type": "error", "code": "MethodNotAllowed",

docs.title: Cancel Order
docs.text:
Cancel Order API

Stop a pending or open order before the exchange executes it. Send the Order ID — the broker cancels it and releases your blocked margin back to your account.

Cancel Food Order= Cancel Order API Restaurant= Broker Server Before Cooking= Before Order Executes Beginner

docs.title: What is Cancel Order?
docs.text:
Think of it like canceling an online food order before the restaurant starts preparing it. If you placed a stock order and it has not been executed yet, you can cancel it using the Cancel Order API — no trade happens, and your money is released.

Food Order Cancel Order2 Pizzas StatusPlaced, Not Cooked ActionCancel before cooking ResultOrder gone, money back ↔ Stock Order Cancel Order10 RELIANCE @ ₹2850 StatusOpen, Not Executed ActionCancel before execution ResultOrder cancelled, margin released

docs.title: Why is Cancel Order Needed?
docs.text: Market conditions changed and the price is no longer attractive Order was placed by mistake (wrong quantity or symbol) A better opportunity is available elsewhere Risk management — remove pending orders during volatile markets Avoid unwanted trades at end of trading session

docs.title: Basic Workflow
docs.text: User ↓ Cancel Order API ↓ Broker Server ↓ Stock Exchange ↓ ✅Order Cancelled

docs.title: What Happens Internally?
docs.text: 1User sends cancel request — with Order ID, Exchange Segment, and User details 2Broker validates — Is the order active? Has it already been executed? Is cancellation allowed? 3Request sent to Exchange — exchange receives the cancellation instruction 4Exchange cancels the order — removes the order from the order book 5Confirmation returned — Order status becomes Cancelled, margin is released Intermediate

docs.title: Which Orders Can Be Cancelled?
docs.text: Open Order BUY RELIANCE @ ₹2850 — Status: Open Order is live in the exchange order book. Can be cancelled. Pending / New Order SELL TCS @ ₹4200 — Status: New Order just placed, not yet matched. Can be cancelled. Completely Filled Order BUY INFY @ ₹1600 — Status: Filled Trade already executed. Cannot be cancelled. Already Cancelled Order Status: Cancelled Order already cancelled. Duplicate request rejected.

docs.title: Common Use Cases
docs.text:
Wrong Order Placement

Accidentally placed 100 shares instead of 10? Cancel the order immediately before it executes.

Market Conditions Changed

Stock price is moving against your expectation. Cancel the pending order and avoid unwanted trades.

Better Price Available

Cancel the existing limit order and place a new one at a better price to improve your entry.

Risk Management

Remove unwanted pending orders during highly volatile sessions to control exposure.

docs.title: Partial Fill Scenario
docs.text:
Original Order 
BUY 100 Shares of RELIANCE
Status = Partially Filled
Executed = 60 Shares
Remaining = 40 Shares
After Cancel Request 
Executed 60 shares → Remain valid
Remaining 40 shares → Cancelled

Final Status: Partially Filled → Cancelled
Margin for 40 shares released back

When you cancel a partially filled order, only the remaining unfilled quantity is cancelled. The already-executed shares are locked and cannot be undone.

docs.text:
Exchange Validation

Before cancelling, the exchange checks the current order status, whether it has already been matched, and whether cancellation is allowed for that order type.

Risk Management System

Broker systems verify user permissions, order ownership, and any exchange-level restrictions before forwarding the cancel request.

Margin Release

After successful cancellation, the funds or margins that were blocked for the order are released back to the user's available balance.

Race Condition

If the order executes at the exact same moment as your cancel request, the cancel may be rejected and the trade will have gone through. Always check the final status.

docs.text:
Funds Overview

Funds represent the money available in your trading account. They determine buying power, margin utilisation, and whether you can place new orders.

Trading Wallet= Funds Credit Limit= Margin Available Blocked Amount= Pending Orders Beginner

docs.title: What are Funds?
docs.text:
Funds are like the wallet of your trading account. They show how much money you have, how much is being used, and how much is still free for trading. Without sufficient funds, orders cannot be placed.

Real-Life Example Total₹1,00,000 In Stocks₹20,000 Blocked₹10,000 Free₹70,000 ↔ Funds API Returns Cash BalanceTotal deposited Used MarginBlocked for trades AvailableReady to trade Buying PowerWith leverage

docs.title: Why are Funds Important?
docs.text: Know how much money is available for trading Manage risk and prevent overtrading Understand margin utilisation at a glance Monitor deposits and withdrawals Check buying power before placing orders Track blocked and available amounts in real time

docs.title: How Funds Flow
docs.text: User Deposits Money ↓ Funds Become Available ↓ User Places Orders ↓ Margin Gets Blocked ↓ Trades Execute ↓ ✅Funds Updated with P&L Intermediate

docs.title: Fund Components
docs.text:
AVAILABLE BALANCE

Amount currently free for placing new orders.

₹1,00,000 − ₹20,000 used = ₹80,000 available UTILISED MARGIN

Amount blocked by open positions and pending orders.

Order requires ₹15,000 → ₹15,000 gets blocked CASH BALANCE

Actual money deposited via bank transfers, profits, or withdrawals.

Bank transfer → Trading account → Cash balance BUYING POWER

Total trading capacity including broker-provided leverage.

₹50,000 × 5× margin = ₹2,50,000 buying power BLOCKED FUNDS

Amounts reserved for pending orders, margin, and fees — released when order executes or cancels.

Buy 100 @ ₹100 → ₹10,000 blocked until fill/cancel PAY-IN / PAY-OUT

Pay-In is money added today. Pay-Out is money withdrawn today.

Deposit ₹25,000 ↑  |  Withdraw ₹10,000 ↓

Loss Reduces Funds

Sold    @ ₹85

→ ₹15 gets DEDUCTED from available balance

docs.title: Advanced Concepts
docs.text:
Margin Leverage

Broker provides extra trading capacity. With 5× leverage, ₹20,000 capital can trade ₹1,00,000 worth of positions.

Realized P&L

Profit from closed trades is added to available funds immediately after the trade settles.

Unrealized P&L

Floating profit/loss on open positions. Not yet in funds — becomes real only when position is closed.

Risk Monitoring

Broker systems continuously check margin, exposure, and losses. Orders are rejected if funds fall below required margin.

docs.title: Common Use Cases
docs.text:
Before Placing Orders

Always check available balance before placing large orders to avoid rejection due to insufficient margin.

Risk Management

Monitor margin utilisation and set alerts when available balance falls below a safe threshold.

Withdrawals

Use Pay-Out field to know the withdrawable balance without disturbing active positions.

Margin Trading

Track leveraged positions — ensure enough buffer so broker does not square off positions automatically.

In Simple Words: Funds represent the money available in a trading account. They determine how much a user can trade, how much margin is used, and how much remains available. The Funds API provides a complete view of cash balance, margin, blocked amounts, and buying power — helping users manage their trading efficiently. Think of Funds as the wallet of your trading account, where money flows in and out as trades execute.

docs.title: P&L Formulas
docs.text:
Realized P&L Profit / loss from closed trades

Locked in when you complete a trade — Buy + Sell same stock.

FORMULA Realized P&L = (Sell Price − Buy Price) × Qty EXAMPLE Bought @₹100 Sold @₹120 Profit+₹20 per share Unrealized P&L Floating profit / loss on open positions

Fluctuates with market price. Not in funds until position is closed.

FORMULA Long  : P&L = (LTP − Avg Buy Price) × Open Qty Short : P&L = (Avg Sell Price − LTP) × Open Qty EXAMPLE (LONG) Bought Reliance @₹2,800 Current LTP₹2,900 Unrealized+₹100 per share

Banking 25% | IT 25% | Pharma 25% | FMCG 25% In Simple Words: A Portfolio is a complete collection of all investments owned by a user. Think of it as a report card for your investments, showing where your money is and how it is performing.

docs.text:
Authentication

Authentication (Auth) is the process of verifying a user's identity before allowing access to Market Data APIs — the security check that confirms you are an authorized user.

Secure access Prevents unauthorized use Account protection API usage control Request tracking Valid users only

docs.title: How Authentication Works
docs.text: Send Login Request → Server Validates → Token Generated → Token Returned → API Access Granted

docs.title: Step 1 — Send Login Request
docs.text:
The user provides credentials:

{ "secretKey": "xxxxx", "appKey": "xxxxx", "source": "WebAPI" }

docs.title: Step 2 — Server Validates Credentials
docs.text:
✔ App Key valid?

Checks if the App Key exists and is active.

✔ Secret Key valid?

Matches the Secret Key against stored records.

✔ Access rights?

Confirms the user has permission to access data.

docs.title: Step 3 — Token Generated & Returned
docs.text:
If validation succeeds, the server returns an access token:

{ "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1Ni..." }

docs.title: Step 4 — Use Token in Future Requests
docs.text:
Include the token in every API request header:

Authorization: Bearer <token>

docs.title: What is an Access Token?
docs.text: WITHOUT TOKEN Login every single API call → WITH TOKEN Login once → use token for all calls

docs.title: Authentication Failure Errors
docs.text: Invalid Credentials "type": "error", "description": "Invalid App Key" Expired Token "type": "error", "description": "Session Expired" Unauthorized Access "type": "error", "description": "Authentication Failed"

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
🔒 Keep Keys Private

Never expose App Key, Secret Key, or Access Token in public code or repositories.

🔐 Use HTTPS

Always communicate through secure encrypted connections.

💾 Store Tokens Securely

Avoid storing tokens in client-side code or public repositories.

🔄 Refresh Expired Sessions

Generate a new token when the current session expires.

Market Depth

Market Depth provides real-time visibility into the full order book — all pending buy and sell orders at every price level. It shows market liquidity, supply and demand, and potential price pressure far beyond the last traded price.

Trading Terminals Liquidity Analysis Support & Resistance Algorithmic Trading Order Flow Analysis Basic

docs.title: What is Market Depth?
docs.text:
The order book is a real-time list of every pending buy and sell order for an instrument. Market Depth shows you the top 5 levels on each side — price, quantity waiting at that price, and how many individual orders are queued there.

Bids (Buy Orders)

Pending orders from buyers. Listed from highest to lowest price. The top bid is the highest a buyer will pay right now.

Green Side Spread

The gap between the best ask and the best bid. A smaller spread means more buyers and sellers are actively trading.

Center Gap Asks (Sell Orders)

Pending orders from sellers. Listed from lowest to highest price. The top ask is the minimum price a seller will accept.

Red Side

Market Depth data uses the same quotes endpoint as touchline data — pass xtsMessageCode: 1502 to receive the 5-level order book instead of just LTP and OHLC.

Wider spread = fewer active traders, higher cost to trade. Liquidity Signal Ask Price ₹2965.60 The lowest price sellers are willing to accept. If you buy at market, you pay this price. docs.title: Reading Market Liquidity
docs.text:
The depth and size of the order book tells you how easily you can execute a large order without moving the market price.

High Liquidity Large quantities on both bid and ask sides. Tight spread. Orders fill quickly at the expected price. Ideal for large orders. Tight spread (₹0.05 – ₹0.20) High total bid/ask quantity Many orders per level Low Liquidity Thin order book with small quantities. Wide spread. Large orders can move the price significantly. Risky for big trades. Wide spread (₹1 – ₹5+) Low total bid/ask quantity Few orders per level

docs.title: Identifying Support and Resistance
docs.text:
Large concentrations of orders at specific price levels can act as support (large buy orders) or resistance (large sell orders).

Support Level A price where a significant number of buy orders are stacked. The market often bounces back up when it reaches this level because buyers absorb selling pressure. 2965.30 — 1,800 qty 2965.20 — 850 qty 2965.00 — 12,000 qty ← Support Resistance Level A price where a significant number of sell orders are stacked. The market often struggles to break above this level because sellers keep absorbing buying pressure. 2970.00 — 15,000 qty ← Resistance 2969.50 — 600 qty 2969.00 — 900 qty

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Combine with Quote Data

Use market depth alongside the last traded price and OHLC to get the complete market picture before placing an order.

Check Liquidity Before Large Orders

Before placing a large order, verify there is enough quantity at the top levels. Thin books can cause significant slippage.

Use WebSocket for Live Updates

Subscribe to event code 1502 via WebSocket instead of polling. Order books update many times per second.

Watch for Order Book Imbalance

A large imbalance in total bid vs ask quantity often signals short-term price direction — more bids = buy pressure, more asks = sell pressure.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Cache the Master File Locally

The master file contains thousands of instruments. Download once at startup and cache in memory — don't re-fetch on every symbol lookup.

Refresh Daily

The master file changes each day (new contracts, expired options). Re-download at market open (9:00 AM) to stay current.

Use Instrument Tokens, Not Names

docs.title: OHLC Data
docs.text:
OHLC Data

The OHLC API provides historical candlestick price data for any tradable instrument — the foundation of every charting system, technical indicator, and backtesting engine. Each candle encodes four prices (Open, High, Low, Close) over a specific time interval.

Candlestick Charts Technical Indicators Backtesting Market Trend Analysis Price Performance Basic

docs.title: What is OHLC?
docs.text:
OHLC stands for Open, High, Low, Close. Each value describes a different price point within a fixed time window — whether that window is 1 minute or 1 day.

O Open The first traded price when the candle interval began. For a daily candle this is the market open price. ₹2940.00 H High The maximum price reached during the entire candle interval. Represents the top of the upper wick. ₹2975.25 L Low The minimum price reached during the entire candle interval. Represents the bottom of the lower wick. ₹2935.80 C Close The last traded price when the candle interval ended. This is the most important price for most indicators. ₹2965.50

docs.title: Candlestick Structure
docs.text: High₹2975.25 Close₹2965.50 Bullish Close > Open Open₹2940.00 Low₹2935.80 Wick (Shadow) Thin vertical lines showing the full High-to-Low range for the interval Green Body (Bullish) Close is higher than Open — price moved up during this interval Red Body (Bearish) Close is lower than Open — price moved down during this interval Intermediate

docs.title: API Endpoint
docs.text:
POST /apimarketdata/instruments/ohlc

Returns historical OHLC candle data for a specific instrument. Pass the exchange segment, instrument ID, time range, and compression interval in the request body.

docs.title: Request and Response
Request Parameters
docs.text: ParameterTypeRequiredDescription exchangeSegmentIntegerYesExchange segment code (1=NSECM, 2=NSEFO, etc.) exchangeInstrumentIDIntegerYesUnique instrument token from the master file startTimeStringYesStart of the historical range — format: Mmm DD YYYY HHMMSS endTimeStringYesEnd of the historical range — same format as startTime compressionValueIntegerYesCandle interval in minutes (see table below)

docs.title: Supported Intervals (compressionValue)
docs.text: 1 1 Minute Intraday scalping, HFT signals 5 5 Minutes Intraday momentum strategies 15 15 Minutes Short-term trend following 30 30 Minutes Intraday support and resistance 60 1 Hour Swing trading, multi-day trends 1440 1 Day Long-term analysis, EOD charts

docs.title: Response Format — Parsed
docs.text:
Split the pipe-separated string on || to get candles, then split each candle on | to get the 7 fields:

0 Timestamp 1718342400 Unix epoch seconds — convert to datetime 1 Open 2940.00 First traded price in interval 2 High 2975.25 Highest price in interval 3 Low 2935.80 Lowest price in interval 4 Close 2965.50 Last traded price in interval 5 Volume 1254789 Total quantity traded 6 Open Interest 0 Outstanding contracts (F&O only) Advanced

docs.title: Technical Analysis with OHLC
docs.text:
Every major technical indicator is derived from OHLC values. Here are the most commonly computed using this data:

Trend Indicators Moving Average (MA) Exponential MA (EMA) MACD SuperTrend Parabolic SAR Momentum Indicators RSI Stochastic Oscillator CCI Williams %R MFI Volatility Indicators Bollinger Bands ATR Keltner Channel Donchian Channel Volume & Price VWAP OBV Support Levels Resistance Levels Pivot Points

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text: 1 Client Application Sends instrument token, time range, and compression interval 2 OHLC API Validates request parameters and routes to historical data store 3 Historical Market Data Fetches tick data, aggregates into OHLC candles by interval 4 OHLC Response Pipe-delimited candle data returned in chronological order 5 Charts and Analytics Parse, render, and compute indicators on the candle array

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Match Interval to Strategy

Use 1-min candles for intraday scalping, 1-day candles for swing trading. Fetching daily candles for a 1-min strategy wastes data resolution.

Request Only What You Need

Narrow the date range to the minimum required. Fetching years of 1-min data is slow and expensive — paginate if you need large historical ranges.

Cache Historical Data

Past candles never change. Once fetched, store them locally and only request the most recent candles on subsequent calls.

Use WebSocket for Live Candles

For the current (in-progress) candle, use WebSocket message code 1505 instead of polling the OHLC endpoint every second.

Quotes

The Quotes API provides real-time market information for tradable instruments — last traded price, bid and ask, open/high/low/close, volume, and market depth. It is the primary source of live pricing data for every application built on the RMoney platform.

docs.title: Market Data Components
docs.text:
Every quote response contains these core price fields. Understanding what each field means is essential before making trading decisions.

LTP Last Traded Price The most recent price at which this instrument was actually traded on the exchange. ₹2965.50 Open Opening Price The first traded price when the exchange opened for the current session. ₹2940.00 High Day High The highest price at which this instrument has traded during the current session. ₹2975.25 Low Day Low The lowest price at which this instrument has traded during the current session. ₹2935.80 Close Previous Close The official closing price from the previous trading session. Used to calculate today's P&L. ₹2938.10 Volume Total Traded Volume The total number of shares or contracts traded from market open to the current moment. 12,54,789

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Use Tokens, Not Symbol Names

Always pass exchangeInstrumentID. Symbol name matching is slower and ambiguous — tokens are exact.

Batch Multiple Instruments

Send all instruments in a single request rather than one call per symbol. Reduces overhead and respects rate limits.

Use WebSocket for High Frequency

For live streaming prices, use WebSocket subscriptions (code 1501/1512) instead of repeated REST polling.

Cache Non-Volatile Fields

Open, previous close, and lot size don't change during the day. Cache them — only poll fields like LTP and volume.

docs.text: WebSocket connections require a valid session token obtained by logging in through the REST API first.

docs.title: Step 1 — Login via REST
docs.text:
from xts_api_client.xts_connect_async import XTSConnect

client = XTSConnect(
    apiKey="your_api_key",
    secretKey="your_secret_key",
    source="WEBAPI",
    root="https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000"
)
await client.marketdata_login()
# client.token and client.userID are now set

docs.title: Step 2 — Connect Market Data WebSocket
docs.text:
from xts_api_client.market_data_socket import MDSocket_io
from xts_api_client.market_data_socket_client import MarketDataSocketClient

class MyPriceFeed(MarketDataSocketClient):
    async def on_connect(self):
        print("Connected to market data feed!")

    async def on_disconnect(self):
        print("Disconnected!")

    async def on_event_last_traded_price_full(self, data):
        print(f"LTP: {data['TradingSymbol']} @ {data['LastTradedPrice']}")

listener = MyPriceFeed()
socket = MDSocket_io(
    token=client.token,
    userID=client.userID,
    root_url=client.root,
    marketdatasocketclient=listener
)
await socket.connect()

interactive_client = XTSConnect(
    apiKey="your_interactive_key",
    secretKey="your_interactive_secret",
    source="WEBAPI",
    root="https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000"
)

order_listener = MyOrderFeed()
order_socket = OrderSocket_io(
    token=interactive_client.token,
    userID=interactive_client.userID,
    root_url=interactive_client.root,
    reconnection=True,
    interativeSocketClient=order_listener
)
await order_socket.connect()

docs.text:
Code Event Bandwidth 1512 LTP only Very low 1501 Touchline (LTP + bid/ask) Low 1502 Full depth (5 levels) Medium 1505 OHLC candle Medium 1510 Open interest Low 1507 Market status Very low

!!! tip Subscribe only to the event codes you actually need. Using 1502 (full depth) for hundreds of instruments simultaneously uses significantly more bandwidth than 1512 (LTP only).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: RMoney provides two WebSocket streams for real-time data. Unlike REST APIs that require repeated polling, WebSockets push data to your application the moment it changes.

docs.title: Two WebSocket Channels
docs.text: Channel Purpose URL Pattern Market Data Socket Live prices, bid/ask, depth, OHLC ticks {root}/?token=...&publishFormat=JSON&broadcastMode=Full Interactive Socket Order updates, trade confirmations, position changes {root}/?token=...&userID=...&apiType=INTERACTIVE

docs.title: When to Use WebSockets vs REST
docs.text: Use Case Recommended Live price feed for a dashboard WebSocket (Market Data) Real-time order status updates WebSocket (Interactive) Fetching historical candles REST (OHLC endpoint) Placing/modifying/cancelling orders REST (Interactive API) One-time instrument lookup REST (Instruments endpoint)

docs.title: Event Codes (Market Data)
docs.text: Code Data 1512 Last Traded Price (LTP) only 1501 Touchline — LTP, Bid, Ask, Volume, OI 1502 Full Market Depth (5 levels) 1505 Live OHLC candle 1510 Open Interest 1507 Market Status (Open / Closed / Pre-open)

docs.title: Subscription Flow
docs.text:
1. Login via REST API  →  receive token
2. Connect WebSocket   →  authenticate with token
3. Subscribe to instruments with event code
4. Receive real-time data in callbacks
5. Unsubscribe / disconnect when done

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Your App
   │
   ├─► REST API ──► Place/Modify/Cancel Orders
   │
   ├─► Market Data WebSocket ──► Price ticks, depth, OHLC
   │
   └─► Interactive WebSocket ──► Order fills, position changes

See Connection for setup and Events for handling data.
